sources.citation: Glottolog 5 reference list for sege1235 (8 refs) and OLAC listing for sbg (Internet Archive copy 2026-02-16)
sources.note: No grammar, sketch or phonology is registered for Seget; OLAC holds only the transnewguinea.org wordlist (from Voorhoeve 1975), Glottolog, Ethnologue and LinguistList entries.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Bibliographic only: lists Animung & Flassy 1987 'Struktur bahasa Seget' (Jakarta: Projek Penelitian Bahasa dan Sastra Indonesia dan Daerah); Flassy 1983 'Bahasa Seget untuk Daftar Holle' (SH); Stokhof & Flassy f/c 'Preliminary note on Seget and related West Bird's Head languages. To appear'; index: Seget -- Barrs 1978, Flassy 1983, SH, Stokhof & Flassy f/c, Voorhoeve 1975, 1982, Wurm & Hattori 1981, 1983.

sources.citation: Holton, Gary & Marian Klamer. 2018. The Papuan languages of East Nusantara and the Bird's Head. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area, 569-640. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on Seget (appears only in the language table); the prosody passage (pp. 587-588) discusses Moskona, Western Pantar, Inanwatan, TAP languages, with no West Bird's Head statement.

sources.citation: Hesse, Ronald G. 1993. Imyan Tehit phonology. MA thesis, University of North Dakota. (scan; references page scanned)
sources.note: Nothing on Seget stress; thesis p. 6 names 'descriptive phonologies and morphologies of.. Seget (Animung and Flassy 1987)' and the References (p. 122) give the full citation of 'Struktur bahasa Seget' -- the lead to the primary description.

sources.citation: Berry, Keith & Christine Berry. 1987. A survey of some West Papuan phylum languages. Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 4: 25-80. Abepura: Cenderawasih University & SIL.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.3 'Phonological features' (pp. 30-32) treats tone (only Abun has it; Table 2 marks Seget 'Tone: x'), syllable count (Seget 24% mono-, 62% di-, 14% trisyllabic), nasal vowels, prenasalised stops, vowel harmony; the word 'stress' does not occur in the volume. Sec. 4.2.2 (p. 40) is sociolinguistic; the 209-item Seget wordlist in the appendix is unmarked for stress.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing; entry 129 Seget lists villages and 'Source: U 4' (an unpublished wordlist).

sources.note: Nothing; p. 719 gives only location and cognate percentages for Seget.
